key_points: Memorial Day, observed on the last Monday in May, honors Americans who died fighting in the nation's wars and traditionally marks the unofficial start of summer.

Arlington National Cemetery's Memorial Day tradition dates back to 1868, and since 1948 soldiers have placed flags at every headstone, with notable burials including two presidents and Challenger astronauts.
The Vietnam Veterans Memorial, designed by 21-year-old Maya Lin and opened in 1982, lists more than 58,000 names of those killed or missing in the war.
Other memorials honor veterans of the Korean War and World War I and II, but there is not yet a national memorial for those who died in the more recent Iraq and Afghanistan wars.
main_idea: Memorial Day honors Americans who died in the nation's wars, and Washington, D.C. is home to several memorials, including Arlington National Cemetery and the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, though newer wars still lack a national memorial.
restate_sentence: It is a day when Americans honor the men and women who have died fighting in America’s wars.
